vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded test credentials seeded into production database. Test user with plaintext password ('password') and hardcoded token ('test_token') can be used to gain unauthorized access. This should never be in committed code.

Command injection vulnerability in execSync call. Arguments are joined directly into shell command string: `execSync(\`gh ${args.join(' ')}\`)`. Malicious arguments can execute arbitrary shell commands. Even with temp file mitigation for body content, other flags/parameters are exposed.

Weak token validation in getUser(). Function accepts any string found in database as valid token without format/length validation. No token expiration or rotation. Any leaked token grants permanent access.
CORS enabled without origin restriction: `app.use(cors())`. Allows requests from any origin. Should specify allowed origins: `cors({ origin: ['https://yourdomain.com'] })`

No input validation for offline queue payload. Arbitrary JSON objects can be stored in AsyncStorage without schema validation. If synced to backend without validation, could introduce data integrity issues or injection attacks.
Missing URL format validation for Supabase endpoint. Environment check only verifies non-empty string, not valid URL format. Malformed URLs could cause unexpected behavior.

recommendations: Remove hardcoded test credentials immediately. Use environment-based test accounts or skip seeding in production builds.
Replace execSync command building with proper argument passing or use safer alternatives like child_process.execFileSync with argument array.
Implement token expiration (JWT with short TTL), validation (format checking), and rotation mechanisms.
Restrict CORS to specific allowed origins instead of '*'. Use: `cors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS?.split(',') })`
Add runtime schema validation for offline queue using zod/joi before storing. Validate structure matches expected action types.
Add URL format validation for Supabase endpoint: `new URL(supabaseUrl)` to throw on invalid format.
Hash passwords in database. Current schema stores plaintext. Use bcrypt with salt.
Add rate limiting to auth endpoints to prevent brute force attacks on token/password.
Remove environment variables from client-side code where possible. Supabase anon key is OK (public), but reconsider architecture if sensitive data depends on it.
Add input validation middleware for all POST/PUT routes before database operations.
